text: I have a clear sense of what I want to achieve in my own life, independently of my family’s expectations.
I can distinguish between opportunities I genuinely want to pursue and those I feel expected to pursue because of my family.
I understand the values that have shaped my family and its approach to business, wealth and responsibility.
I have considered which of those values I want to carry forward and which I would approach differently.
I have thought seriously about what family wealth means for my own identity, choices and responsibilities.
I can discuss the privileges and responsibilities associated with family wealth without taking them for granted or feeling defined by them.
I have a reasonably clear idea of the role, if any, I would like to play in the family enterprise or family wealth.
I believe I could pursue a fulfilling life even if my eventual role within the family were different from what is currently expected.
I understand how the family’s principal businesses and wealth were created.
I understand the important decisions, successes, failures and turning points that shaped the family’s present position.
I understand how the family’s principal business interests actually make money and what could threaten them.
I understand the major strategic challenges and opportunities facing the family enterprise over the next decade.
I know who the principal executives, advisers and other important non-family stakeholders are and understand their roles.
I understand where important knowledge and decision-making authority currently sit within the family enterprise.
I understand the interests, expectations and potential concerns of the principal branches and generations of the family.
I understand how changes in ownership, leadership or family circumstances could affect relationships within the wider family.
I understand what the family owns and, broadly, how those assets are held.
I understand the difference between being an owner, a beneficiary, a director, an executive and a trustee or fiduciary.
I can read and understand the principal financial information needed to make informed decisions as an owner.
I understand the basic relationship between return, risk, liquidity, concentration and diversification.
I understand the purpose of the principal companies, trusts, foundations, holding structures or other vehicles relevant to me.
I understand the principal rights, restrictions and responsibilities that would accompany my future ownership or beneficial interests.
I have developed my own principles for spending, investing, giving and preserving capital.
I would feel able to question an investment, transaction or recommendation even when it was proposed by an experienced family member or professional adviser.
I understand how significant family, ownership and business decisions are currently made.
I know which decisions belong to management, owners, boards, trustees, family bodies or individual family members.
I can express a different view respectfully when I disagree with a senior family member.
I feel able to ask questions about matters I do not understand without worrying that this will be interpreted as weakness or disloyalty.
I can separate family relationships from the responsibilities involved in making ownership or business decisions.
I have experience reaching decisions with people whose interests, personalities or priorities differ from my own.
I understand what good boards, family councils or other governance bodies are supposed to achieve.
I have had meaningful exposure to formal meetings in which significant business, investment, ownership or family decisions are made.
I have developed meaningful experience or expertise outside the protection of the family environment.
I have experienced situations in which my performance was judged independently of my family name or relationships.
I have been responsible for decisions whose consequences affected other people, capital or an organisation.
I have experienced failure, criticism or significant setbacks and can identify what I learned from them.
I am deliberately developing the skills I would need for the family responsibilities I may eventually assume.
I receive useful feedback from people who can challenge me objectively rather than simply reassure me.
I know when a decision requires expertise that I do not personally possess.
I feel capable of selecting, questioning and, where necessary, replacing professional advisers.
I understand what the current generation expects from me over the next five to ten years.
The current generation understands what I want for myself rather than relying on assumptions about my future role.
There is a realistic process through which I can gradually acquire greater responsibility rather than receiving it suddenly.
I have opportunities to practise making meaningful decisions before I am expected to make consequential ones alone.
I know what would be expected of me if a senior family member suddenly became unable to act.
I know whom I would contact and what immediate responsibilities I might have if an unexpected family, business or ownership crisis occurred.
I have considered what I would want to preserve, change or create if I eventually had significant influence over the family’s wealth or enterprise.
I believe I could assume greater responsibility without feeling that I had to become a copy of the generation before me.
